thread:
Alex K: Quick follow-up from the ATTn kernel RFC — we're seeing more divergence in triton vs CUTLASS paths than I expected. Want to align on what we carry forward and what becomes 'experimental'.
Mira S: Can you summarize where we diverge? memory/layout, launch configs, or algorithmic changes?
Alex K: Short list: (1) kernel interface (scratch vs preallocated KV), (2) block layout / smem tiling assumptions, (3) fused rotary+softmax microkernels that Triton optimizes differently, (4) tiling for long context (KV split).
Samir: From my local runs: Triton path wins latency at 2k seq for batch=1, but CUTLASS has more predictable GPU mem for larger batches. Quick numbers: 
```
# rough microbench
model=attn32
batch=1 seq=2048 -> triton: p50 95ms, mem 6.8GB
batch=8 seq=512  -> cutlass: p50 42ms, mem 10.1GB
```
Mira S: Those are useful. Do we have any failing regressions on long-tail prompts with Triton?
Samir: One reproducible OOM with Triton when context fragmentation happens (long prompt + many cached KV slices). CUTLASS fell back slower but didn't OOM.
Jorge P: Proposed operational stance: make CUTLASS the safety fallback for Dedicated/Private; Triton as default for Hosted where latency matters, but mark Triton 'opt-in high-performance' in config. Action items: 1) define kernel interface stability guarantees, 2) add memory-safety mode for Triton, 3) rollout/canary plan. Thoughts?
Liz H: +1 to safety fallback. We need clear telemetry flags: which model, kernel variant, reason for fallback. Product wants to show deterministic SLOs.
Alex K: Ok. For (1) kernel interface: let's freeze a minimal ABI: allocate_kv(prealloc=true|false), step(batch, kv_ptr, qkv_layout), release_kv. Keep it small so both runtimes can implement.
Mira S: For (2) memory-safety mode — proposal: conservative tiling + prefetch eviction threshold. Implementation idea: runtime tracks per-request worst-case KV size and rejects/forces fallback if estimated_total_kv > pool_ahead_limit.
Samir: I can prototype an estimator. Two quick heuristics: a) per-layer fixed KV bytes by seq_len b) dynamic sampled run tracking. Will try a) first.
Jorge P: Rollout plan suggestion: week 1 internal perf run comparing both on a suite of 100 prompts; week 2 canary on 5% hosted traffic with auto-fallback; week 3 promote or rollback. I'll own the canary playbook.
Liz H: Add a communication item for customers on Dedicated — we may need an opt-in toggle if they want Triton experimental kernels.
ci-bot: CI: kernel-integration-tests passed on main (artifact: gcs://rbw-ci/attn-kernel/1893456789). :white_check_mark:
Mira S: Small API nit: use explicit 'compatibility_level' field in model config (v1=stable-abi, v2=experimental-kernels) so we can roll models across runtimes without mismatched expectations.
Alex K: Good call. Final quick list of action items (short):
- Samir: prototype KV-size estimator + perf runs (due +4d)
- Jorge: canary playbook + metrics (due +5d)
- Mira: draft kernel-ABI doc + compatibility_level spec (due +3d)
- Liz: customer opt-in text + UI checkbox for Dedicated (due +7d)
- Alex: add runtime fallback hooks and telemetry events (due +6d)
Please reply with conflicts or if you want to own different items.
Samir: I can also try a tiny Triton memory-safety patch while prototyping.
Jorge P: I'll schedule the internal perf run Friday.
Mira S: I'll start the ABI doc now and drop a link here when draft is up.
Liz H: noted, will draft customer-facing copy next week.
Alex K: Thanks all — let's regroup after the initial perf runs. :thumbsup:
